newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein easier in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein easier in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm oil prices were easier in late trading on Friday on the back of thin buying interest, traders said.
They said olein was lower in Jakarta at 1,430-35 rupiah/kg against the morning's price of 1,435-40 rupiah, but offers were also heard at 1,430 rupiah.
The traders said state logistics agency BULOG continued its market operation to control the price of cooking oil ahead of the Eid-al Fitr celebration and sold olein at 1,430 rupiah/kg.
Refiners have said there was no margin in processing olein due to the relatively high price of crude palm oil.
Traders in the north Sumatran city of Medan said crude palm oil was done at the equivalent of 1,255 rupiah/kg at a 1000-tonne tender. Crude palm oil was last done at 1,250 rupiah.
"The market is still weak because of the fasting month of Ramadan. We expect the prices to stay in the same range next week," said one trader.
The trader said an estimation on Friday showing that palm oil exports increased to 180,000 tonnes in December against 170,000 tonnes in November had little impact to the market.
"There's nothing significant on the figure, because it's quite a weak export," said the trader.
Traders said the market was instead influenced by developments in the Malaysian market. Malaysian palm oil prices eased at midday on speculation of poor January export data.
Traders said they expected demand to pick up next week and prices to move up slightly. "We expect there will be a little bit of fluctuation of prices next week," said one trader.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MV Asean Trader will leave for South Korea on Sunday with 3,000 tonnes of palm kernel expeller, while the MV Ozge Akosy will leave for Europe on January 31 with 22,400 tonnes of palm kernel expeller.
The KM Pershing will leave on Sunday for Tanjung Priok, Jakarta, with 1,192 tonnes of olein. The MT Istana I will leave on Saturday for Cirebon with 1,700 tonnes of olein.
